title: Clearing denominators of sections on the nonvanishing locus, qcqs case
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] (the intersection of any two affine opens is quasi-compact), $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $X_s=\{x\in X:s(x)\ne0\text{ in }\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)\}$, where $\kappa(x)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. For every $u\in\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal F)$ there exist $m\ge0$ and $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$ such that $t|_{X_s}=u\otimes(s|_{X_s})^{\otimes m}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (label lemma-invert-s-sections), proof of part (2): surjectivity of the canonical localization map

proof.text: At each point choose a Zariski neighbourhood on which $\mathcal L$ is free by [def-sc-invertible-module], and an affine neighbourhood on which $\mathcal F$ is a tilde module by [pqf-def-coherent]. Choose a principal open inside the affine presentation neighbourhood and the trivializing neighbourhood; [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] identifies the restriction of the tilde module there with the localization of its presenting module, so both properties hold on this principal open. These opens cover $X$, so quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] gives a finite subcover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^r V_i$ on which both properties hold. Write $e_i$ for a generator and $s|_{V_i}=f_i e_i$. For a point of $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, the image of $s$ in $\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)$ is nonzero exactly when $f_i\notin\mathfrak p_x$; hence $X_s\cap V_i=D(f_i)$. Write $\mathcal F|_{V_i}=\widetilde M_i$; identifying $M_i$ with $\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal F)$ by the $r=1$ case of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], that same node identifies $\Gamma(D(f_i),\mathcal F)$ with $(M_i)_{f_i}$. Write $u|_{D(f_i)}=v_i/f_i^{a_i}$, choose $a\ge a_i$ for every $i$, and set $w_i=f_i^{a-a_i}v_i\otimes e_i^{\otimes a}\in\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes a})$. Then $w_i|_{D(f_i)}=u|_{D(f_i)}\otimes s^{\otimes a}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections), part (2), finite trivializing cover and local fractions

proof.text: For each pair $i,j$, put $W_{ij}=V_i\cap V_j$. It is quasi-compact by quasi-separatedness of $X$; it is quasi-separated since every two affine opens of the open subscheme $W_{ij}$ are affine opens of $X$ and have quasi-compact intersection. The difference $d_{ij}=w_i|_{W_{ij}}-w_j|_{W_{ij}}$ is a section of $\mathcal G_{ij}=(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes a})|_{W_{ij}}$, which is quasi-coherent by [lem-sc-invertible-tensor-qcoherent]. On $(W_{ij})_s=W_{ij}\cap X_s$ both restrictions equal $u\otimes s^{\otimes a}$ by Step 1, so $d_{ij}$ restricts to zero. Apply [lem-sc-p1-section-restriction-s-torsion] to the qcqs scheme $W_{ij}$, its invertible module $\mathcal L|_{W_{ij}}$, its section $s|_{W_{ij}}$, and $\mathcal G_{ij}$: for some $b_{ij}\ge0$, multiplication by $s^{\otimes b_{ij}}$ kills $d_{ij}$ on $W_{ij}$.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections), part (2), compatibility on quasi-compact overlaps

proof.text: There are finitely many pairs, so choose $b\ge b_{ij}$ for all of them. Multiplying each $w_i$ by $s^{\otimes b}$ gives $z_i\in\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes(a+b)})$. On $W_{ij}$ their difference is $s^{\otimes(b-b_{ij})}(s^{\otimes b_{ij}}d_{ij})=0$ by Step 2. The sheaf gluing axiom gives a global section $t$ restricting to $z_i$ on every $V_i$. On $D(f_i)$, Step 1 gives $z_i=u\otimes s^{\otimes(a+b)}$; these opens cover $X_s$, so $t|_{X_s}=u\otimes s^{\otimes(a+b)}$. Take $m=a+b$.

split_report.summary: Proved the qcqs clearing-denominators statement by finitely many affine charts with simultaneous line-bundle trivializations and module presentations, affine module localization, power-torsion on each quasi-compact overlap, and gluing. The overlap step uses the existing restriction-torsion statement for quasi-coherent modules and does not assume affine intersections. No new nodes were needed.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes lem-sc-p1-graded-resolution's proof clause comparing graded sections on the nonvanishing open with localized global sections, via lem-sc-p1-invertible-section-localization: Step 1 lifts local fractions, Step 2 clears overlap differences, Step 3 glues a global section.

tool_uses.why: The overlap argument uses its quasi-coherence conclusion for the twisted module; this is a generic tensor-product tool in another unit.
